newsitem.title: USA: Brushfires burning in parched southern California.
newsitem.headline: Brushfires burning in parched southern California.

text.p: Scorching temperatures and high winds sparked a series of brushfires in parched areas of southern California on Friday, causing a massive traffic jam as people fled Los Angeles for the long holiday weekend.
Residents were evacuated from some 45 homes and also the Disney Ranch, where TV shows and movies are made, as 350 firefighters battled to keep the blazes away from homes.
In the air, 17 water-dropping helicopters and two fixed-wing tanker aircraft made runs over the fires.

The California Highway patrol temporarily closed part of the Interstate highway 14 or Antelope Valley Freeway near Santa Clarita, some 30 miles (45 km) north of Los Angeles, where one fire scorched more than 400 acres (160 hectares) of scrubland.
One air tanker reportedly dropped a load of chemical fire retardant on the surface of the road to prevent the fire from jumping across to the more heavily residential west side.

Traffic preparing for the American Independence Day holiday was driven into chaos as drivers sought alternative routes to get to the main north-south Interstate highway 5, or Golden State Freeway that links Los Angeles and San Diego with San Francisco and Sacramento.

With temperatures hovering around 100 degrees (38 degress C) in Los Angeles and even higher in the valleys and deserts, the brushfire danger has risen. At least three other fires were burning in the northern suburbs of Los Angeles, where there has been no rain for months.
One big blaze in the San Gabriel mountains near Azusa has burned more than 1,500 acres in the Angeles National Forest but was expected to be fully contained by the weekend.

The smoke from the fires increased the normal smog in the Los Angeles basin, causing health authorities to issue a stage one smog alert. People were advised to stay indoors and avoid vigorous activities that might cause breathing problems.
